newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Nizhnetagilsk steel plant plans ADR.
newsitem.headline: Russian Nizhnetagilsk steel plant plans ADR.

text.p: Russian steel maker AO Nizhnetagilsky Metallurgichesky Kombinat plans to issue Level One American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) or privately-placed 144-A ADRs as soon as November, the company's chief lawyer said on Wednesday.

"We expect that a debut on the international financial market will allow Nizhnetagilsk not only to bring its share price to a level commensurate to its value but also to improve the image of the company in order to attract credits," legal division head Nikolai Korepanov told Reuters.

"The company will choose an investment consultant by the end of July and after three months the issue will be registered and ready," Korepanov said. Alfred Berg, Renaissance Capital and Brunswick are being considered among others, he added.

Nizhnetagilsk, one of Russia's largest steel makers located in the Ural mountains region of Russia on the western edge of Siberia, has already held talks with the Bank of New York for it to act as depositary.
Coopers & Lybrand have almost completed an audit of 1996 results to international accounting standards and a separate auditor, Enterprises, is completing accounts for 1994 and 1995, he said.
ADRs which cover local shares of the steel maker would trade on foreign exchanges. Nizhnetagilsk shares on the Russian Trading System rose to $0.144 at 1258 GMT from $0.122 at the close on Tuesday.
